groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: At the baggage service desk

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: Excuse me, my suitcase never came out on the belt. I was on flight KR 218 from Hallington.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: Here it is. It's a large silver case with a cracked wheel and a red name tag on the handle.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.text: Thanks. According to our system, it was loaded onto a connecting flight by mistake. It should arrive on the evening flight.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: ___2___ I've got a job interview first thing tomorrow, and my suit is in there.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.text: I completely understand. ___3___ we'll deliver the case straight to your hotel by ten tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Nadia
dialogue.text: That would be a huge help. Thank you.

options: Would you like to check in another bag?
How long are you planning to stay here?
Could I see your baggage claim tag, please?
Did you enjoy the meal on the flight?
Is this your first time flying with us?
items.explanationTh: เจ้าหน้าที่ต้องขอหลักฐานก่อน และ Nadia ตอบว่า "Here it is" แล้วบรรยายกระเป๋า จึงต้องเป็นการขอดูป้ายรับกระเป๋า (baggage claim tag) ตัวเลือกอื่นไม่เกี่ยวกับการตามหากระเป๋า

options: Then I'd rather fly home tonight.
Then I'll just carry it with me.
So it's already at my hotel?
In that case, there's no rush at all.
That's cutting it a bit fine, though.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคถัดมาบอกว่าพรุ่งนี้เช้ามีสัมภาษณ์งานและชุดสูทอยู่ในกระเป๋า แสดงว่ากังวลว่าเวลาเฉียดฉิวเกินไป "cutting it a bit fine" ส่วน "there's no rush at all" (ไม่ต้องรีบเลย) ขัดกับความกังวลนี้

options: Unless you fill in this form,
Instead of filling in this form,
Even though you filled in this form,
If you fill in this form,
Until you had filled in this form,
items.explanationTh: การส่งกระเป๋าถึงโรงแรมเป็นผลที่เกิดเมื่อกรอกแบบฟอร์ม จึงใช้เงื่อนไข "If you fill in this form, we'll deliver..." ส่วน Unless ให้ความหมายตรงข้าม

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Planning a rehearsal

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Ken, we still haven't picked a time to rehearse our presentation. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Ken
dialogue.text: Thursday's tricky. I've got badminton practice until five. Could we make it Friday lunchtime instead?

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: Friday's fine by me, but Arthit said he's ___2___ with the school magazine all week.

dialogue.speaker: Ken
dialogue.text: Then let's each record our parts separately, and he can add his on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: Ploy
dialogue.text: ___3___ The teacher wants to watch us rehearse together, remember?

dialogue.speaker: Ken
dialogue.text: Good point. I'll message him tonight and ask whether he can spare twenty minutes.

options: When was the presentation due?
Where did you save the slides?
Why did you choose that topic again?
Who presented first last week?
How does Thursday after school sound?
items.explanationTh: Ploy ต้องการนัดเวลาซ้อม และ Ken ตอบว่า "Thursday's tricky" จึงต้องเป็นการเสนอวันพฤหัสบดี ตัวเลือกอื่นไม่ได้เสนอเวลา

options: run out
put off
tied up
taken after
given in
items.explanationTh: "be tied up with something" แปลว่ายุ่งหรือติดธุระกับงานนั้น เหมาะกับการที่ Arthit ทำนิตยสารโรงเรียนทั้งสัปดาห์ ส่วน put off = เลื่อน, run out = หมด, take after = เหมือน, give in = ยอมแพ้

options: Same here, I'm free on Saturday.
I'm not sure that would work.
Sure, go ahead and record it.
That's exactly what I had in mind.
You can say that again.
items.explanationTh: ประโยคถัดมาให้เหตุผลคัดค้านว่าครูต้องการเห็นซ้อมพร้อมกัน จึงต้องเป็นการไม่เห็นด้วยอย่างสุภาพ ตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นการเห็นด้วยทั้งหมด

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Returning a faulty product

dialogue.speaker: Lukas
dialogue.text: Hi. I bought these wireless headphones here last week, but the left side keeps cutting out.

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm sorry about that. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Lukas
dialogue.text: Yes, it's right here. I'd prefer a replacement rather than a refund, if possible.

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, that model is ___2___ at the moment. We won't get any more until next month.

dialogue.speaker: Lukas
dialogue.text: I see. In that case, ___3___

dialogue.speaker: Assistant
dialogue.text: Of course. The ones on the second shelf are the same price, and you're welcome to try them first.

options: Do you need a bigger size?
Shall I charge them overnight?
Would you like them gift-wrapped?
Could you turn the volume down?
Have you still got the receipt?
items.explanationTh: Lukas ตอบว่า "Yes, it's right here." แสดงว่าถูกถามถึงสิ่งของที่พกมา คือใบเสร็จ ซึ่งร้านต้องใช้เมื่อคืนสินค้า

options: on the house
in good shape
out of order
up to date
out of stock
items.explanationTh: ประโยคต่อมา "We won't get any more until next month" แสดงว่าสินค้าหมด จึงใช้ out of stock ส่วน out of order ใช้กับเครื่องที่เสีย และ on the house แปลว่าฟรี

options: I'd rather just keep these ones.
could I swap them for a similar pair?
I'm glad they're working perfectly now.
could you repair them while I wait?
I'll ask for a replacement, then.
items.explanationTh: เมื่อรุ่นเดิมหมด ทางเลือกที่สมเหตุสมผลคือขอเปลี่ยนเป็นรุ่นใกล้เคียง และพนักงานตอบว่ารุ่นบนชั้นที่สองราคาเท่ากันและลองได้ ซึ่งไม่เข้ากับการขอซ่อมหรือเก็บของเดิมไว้ ส่วนการขอ replacement รุ่นเดิมทำไม่ได้แล้ว

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: Calling a bike shop

dialogue.speaker: Wanda
dialogue.text: Pedal Point Repairs, Wanda speaking. How can I help?

dialogue.speaker: Tomas
dialogue.text: Hi. My bike's chain keeps slipping, and the brakes ___1___ quite a lot when I stop.

dialogue.speaker: Wanda
dialogue.text: That sounds like a fairly quick job. ___2___

dialogue.speaker: Tomas
dialogue.text: Would tomorrow morning be all right? I need it for my commute on Monday.

dialogue.speaker: Wanda
dialogue.text: Tomorrow's fully booked, I'm afraid, but if you drop it off this afternoon, ___3___

dialogue.speaker: Tomas
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll be there around three.

options: squeaking
to squeak
has squeaked
squeaks
squeak
items.explanationTh: ประธาน "the brakes" เป็นพหูพจน์และเล่าสิ่งที่เกิดเป็นประจำ จึงใช้ Present Simple รูปไม่เติม s คือ squeak

options: How much did you pay for the bike?
Why don't you buy a new chain online?
Where did you learn to ride?
Who sold you that bike originally?
When would you like to bring it in?
items.explanationTh: Tomas ตอบด้วยการเสนอเวลา "Would tomorrow morning be all right?" คำถามที่เหมาะจึงเป็นการถามว่าจะนำจักรยานมาเมื่อไร

options: it had been ready by Saturday
it'll be ready by Saturday
it was ready by Saturday
it would have been ready by Saturday
it has been ready since Saturday
items.explanationTh: ประโยคเงื่อนไขแบบที่ 1 (If + present, will + V1) เพราะพูดถึงสิ่งที่เป็นไปได้ในอนาคต จึงใช้ "it'll be ready"

groups.instructionTh: อ่านบทสนทนา แล้วเลือกคำตอบที่เหมาะสมที่สุดเติมในช่องว่าง
groups.title: University open day

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: Hi, I'm interested in the marine biology programme. ___1___

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: Yes, Dr. Orvel is giving a talk in Hall C at two. Students can ask her questions afterwards.

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: Great. And ___2___ any scholarships for international applicants?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.text: There are a few. ___3___ Everything you need is in this booklet, including the deadlines.

dialogue.speaker: Mai
dialogue.text: Thanks so much. That's really helpful.

options: Is there anyone I could talk to about it?
Could you tell me what time it is?
Have you ever studied marine biology?
Do you happen to know how to swim?
How far is the nearest beach from here?
items.explanationTh: เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบว่ามีอาจารย์บรรยายและให้ถามคำถามได้ จึงแสดงว่า Mai ถามหาคนที่จะพูดคุยเรื่องหลักสูตรด้วย

options: could you tell me if are there
do you know whether is there
do you happen to know are there
would you happen to know there are
would you happen to know if there are
items.explanationTh: คำถามทางอ้อมหลัง "would you happen to know" ต้องมี if/whether และเรียงประธานก่อนกริยา (if there are) ตัวเลือกอื่นขาด if หรือกลับกริยาไว้หน้าประธานแบบคำถามตรง

options: Don't bother applying this year.
I'm afraid we've never had any.
Take one of these with you.
You'd better ask somebody else.
They're only for local students, though.
items.explanationTh: เจ้าหน้าที่ตอบว่ามีทุนอยู่บ้าง และต่อด้วย "Everything you need is in this booklet" จึงต้องเป็นการยื่นเอกสารให้ ตัวเลือกอื่นขัดกับข้อมูล เช่น ทุนมีสำหรับผู้สมัครต่างชาติ ไม่ใช่เฉพาะนักเรียนในประเทศ

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Linden Court lease notice
groups.text:
NOTICE TO RESIDENTS: LINDEN COURT APARTMENTS
Lease Renewals for the Coming Year

All current leases at Linden Court expire on 31 March. Residents who wish to stay must return the signed renewal form to the management office by 15 February. Late forms cannot be guaranteed, as vacant units will be advertised to the public from 16 February.

Please note the following changes under the new lease:
• Monthly rent will rise by 4%, the first increase in three years.
• Tenants may now keep one small pet (under 10 kg) with written permission from the office.
• Bicycles must be stored in the basement rack, not on balconies or in corridors.

Residents planning to move out must give at least 30 days' written notice so that a final inspection can be arranged. Deposits will be returned within 14 days of a satisfactory inspection.

Linden Court Management

items.stem: What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To advertise empty apartments to the general public
To warn tenants about a recent rise in break-ins
To explain how and when residents can renew their leases
To announce that the building is going to be sold
To invite residents to a meeting about keeping pets
items.explanationTh: ประกาศมีหัวเรื่อง "Lease Renewals" และบอกกำหนดส่งแบบฟอร์มต่อสัญญาพร้อมเงื่อนไขใหม่ จุดประสงค์หลักจึงเป็นการแจ้งวิธีและกำหนดต่อสัญญาเช่า

items.stem: What may happen to a resident who returns the renewal form on 20 February?
options: Their flat may already have been offered to someone else.
They will be charged a late fee of 4% of the rent.
Their deposit will be returned within 14 days.
They will have to move their bicycle to the basement.
They will be asked to leave before 31 March.
items.explanationTh: ประกาศบอกว่าแบบฟอร์มที่ส่งช้า "cannot be guaranteed" เพราะห้องว่างจะถูกประกาศให้คนทั่วไปตั้งแต่ 16 ก.พ. จึงอาจมีคนอื่นได้ห้องไปแล้ว

items.stem: Which statement about the rent is true?
options: It will go down by 4% after 31 March.
It goes up by 4% every single year.
It has stayed the same for the past three years.
Tenants who keep a pet will pay more of it.
It must be paid in person at the basement office.
items.explanationTh: ข้อความ "the first increase in three years" แสดงว่าค่าเช่าไม่ได้ขึ้นมาสามปีแล้ว ไม่ใช่ขึ้นทุกปีหรือลดลง

items.stem: The word "vacant" in the notice is closest in meaning to ____.
options: expensive
empty
shared
renovated
furnished
items.explanationTh: ห้องที่จะนำไปประกาศหาผู้เช่าใหม่คือห้องที่ไม่มีคนอยู่ vacant จึงแปลว่า empty (ว่าง)

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Laundry instructions
groups.text:
SUDSWAY 24-HOUR LAUNDRY: HOW TO USE OUR MACHINES

1. Load your clothes, close the door firmly and choose a programme. Do not fill the drum more than three-quarters full.
2. Pay at the central kiosk with coins or the SudsWay app. Enter the number printed on your machine's door, not the number painted on the floor in front of it.
3. Washing takes 35 minutes. Dryers run in 12-minute cycles; extra cycles can be added at the kiosk.

Please collect your laundry within 15 minutes of the cycle ending. After that, staff or other customers may move it to the shelves by the window.

Detergent is added automatically. Customers who bring their own must select the ECO setting, which skips our detergent and costs 10 baht less.

Machine not working? Call the number above the kiosk. Refunds are processed within 48 hours.

items.stem: What should a customer with a very large load of washing do?
options: Press it down firmly before closing the door
Divide it so that no drum is overfilled
Choose the ECO setting to save money
Ask a member of staff to load it
Pay for an extra cycle at the kiosk
items.explanationTh: ป้ายบอกว่า "Do not fill the drum more than three-quarters full" ผ้าจำนวนมากจึงต้องแบ่งใส่หลายเครื่องเพื่อไม่ให้ถังแน่นเกินไป

items.stem: Why might a customer accidentally pay for the wrong machine?
options: They forgot to close the door firmly.
They entered the number on the floor.
They paid with the app instead of coins.
They selected the ECO programme.
They collected their laundry too late.
items.explanationTh: ป้ายเตือนให้ใส่หมายเลขที่ประตูเครื่อง "not the number painted on the floor" แสดงว่าหมายเลขบนพื้นอาจไม่ตรงกับเครื่องและทำให้จ่ายผิดเครื่องได้

items.stem: A customer who brings her own detergent ____.
options: should add it after the first 35 minutes
is not allowed to use the washing machines
must pay an extra 10 baht at the kiosk
should select ECO and will pay 10 baht less
needs written permission from a staff member
items.explanationTh: ป้ายระบุว่าผู้ที่นำผงซักฟอกมาเอง "must select the ECO setting, which skips our detergent and costs 10 baht less"

items.stem: Kai's dryer finished at 6:00 p.m., but he came back at 6:30 p.m. What may have happened?
options: His clothes may have been washed again.
His clothes may have been moved to a shelf.
He may have been charged for extra time.
His dryer may have started another cycle.
He may have received a 48-hour refund.
items.explanationTh: Kai กลับมาช้ากว่า 15 นาทีหลังเครื่องหยุด ป้ายบอกว่าหลังจากนั้น "staff or other customers may move it to the shelves by the window" ส่วนการคิดเงินเพิ่มหรือคืนเงินไม่เกี่ยวกับกรณีนี้

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: An email from the fair coordinator
groups.text:
Subject: Science Fair: change to the judging format

Dear participants,

Thank you for registering for this year's Hillcrest Science Fair on 14 March. Sixty-two projects have been entered, almost double last year's number. While this is wonderful news, it also means we need to change the way judging works.

In previous years, each judge visited every table for ten minutes. With sixty-two projects, that would keep a single judge busy for more than ten hours, so this year the judges will work in three panels, each responsible for one category: life sciences, physical sciences or engineering. Please check the attached list to confirm that your project has been placed in the right category. If you believe it has not, email me by 1 March with a short explanation; after that date, the list will be final.

Several of you have asked whether posters must be printed. They do not, but if you plan to use a screen instead, you will need to bring your own device with a fully charged battery. There are only a handful of power points in the hall, and they will be reserved for projects that genuinely need electricity to run.

Finally, a reminder that the judges are interested in your process, not just your results. A project whose experiment "failed" but which explains clearly what went wrong, and why, can score just as highly as one that worked perfectly.

Best wishes,
Daniel Achebe
Science Fair Coordinator

items.stem: What is the main purpose of Mr. Achebe's email?
options: To complain about projects submitted late
To explain changes caused by a rise in entries
To announce that the fair has been postponed
To ask students to help judge other projects
To invite more students to enter the fair
items.explanationTh: อีเมลบอกว่ามีโครงงานเกือบสองเท่าของปีก่อน "it also means we need to change the way judging works" แล้วอธิบายรูปแบบการตัดสินใหม่และข้อปฏิบัติ

items.stem: Why will the judges work in three panels this year?
options: Some categories had no projects at all last year.
One judge could not see every project in a reasonable time.
The hall is too small for all the project tables.
The judges disagreed about last year's winners.
Students asked to be judged by subject experts.
items.explanationTh: ถ้ากรรมการคนเดียวดูทุกโต๊ะ "that would keep a single judge busy for more than ten hours" จึงต้องแบ่งเป็นสามคณะตามหมวด

items.stem: A student emails on 5 March to say his project is in the wrong category. What will most likely happen?
options: He will have to present a printed poster instead.
His project will be moved to another category at once.
His project will stay in the category on the list.
He will be asked to withdraw from the fair.
His project will be judged by all three panels.
items.explanationTh: ต้องแจ้งภายใน 1 มีนาคม "after that date, the list will be final" การแจ้งวันที่ 5 มีนาคมจึงสายเกินไป โครงงานน่าจะอยู่ในหมวดเดิม

items.stem: The phrase "a handful of" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ____.
options: some broken
hand-operated
only a few
a great many
several new
items.explanationTh: ผู้เขียนให้นำแบตเตอรี่มาเองเพราะปลั๊กมีน้อยและสงวนไว้ให้โครงงานที่จำเป็น a handful of จึงหมายถึงจำนวนน้อย (only a few)

items.stem: According to the email, what do the judges care about?
options: Whether the posters were printed professionally
How many power points each project uses
How much the equipment for a project cost
How clearly students explain their process
Whether the experiment gave the expected result
items.explanationTh: ย่อหน้าสุดท้ายบอกว่า "the judges are interested in your process, not just your results" และโครงงานที่ล้มเหลวแต่อธิบายได้ชัดก็ได้คะแนนสูงได้

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Lost on purpose
groups.text:
Lost on Purpose: My Month Without a Map App
Posted by Nicha, 17

Last month, I deleted the map app from my phone. My friends thought I'd lost my mind, and to be fair, the first week gave them plenty of evidence. I missed the start of my cousin's birthday lunch because I mixed up two streets with almost identical names, and I spent forty minutes circling the old city looking for a stationery shop that turned out to be directly behind my school.

So why did I do it? Earlier this year, I realised that I could get to dozens of places around Chiang Mai, yet I couldn't have drawn even a rough sketch of how any of them connected. I was following a blue dot, not learning a city.

By the second week, things began to change. I bought a folding paper map, and before going anywhere, I traced the route with my finger and picked out two or three landmarks: a temple gate, a petrol station, a tall tamarind tree. I also started asking people for directions, which I'd always found awkward. Most were happy to help, and one fruit seller even drew me a little map on the back of a receipt.

Now that the month is over, I've reinstalled the app. I'm not going to pretend paper is always better; for a bus journey across town, the app wins easily. But I use it differently. I check the route first, then put my phone away and try to get there on my own.

items.stem: Why did Nicha decide to delete her map app?
options: Her friends had challenged her to try it.
She wanted to cut down on her mobile data.
The app had given her the wrong directions.
She noticed she didn't understand how places connected.
Her phone had run out of space for new apps.
items.explanationTh: Nicha เล่าว่าไปได้หลายที่แต่ "couldn't have drawn even a rough sketch of how any of them connected" คือไม่เข้าใจว่าสถานที่ต่าง ๆ เชื่อมกันอย่างไร

items.stem: What does Nicha mean by "the first week gave them plenty of evidence"?
options: She quickly proved that her friends were wrong.
Her friends helped her find her way that week.
Her early mistakes seemed to prove her friends right.
Her friends also got lost during the first week.
She showed her friends how well she could navigate.
items.explanationTh: เพื่อนคิดว่าเธอเสียสติ และสัปดาห์แรกเธอหลงทางจนไปงานสายและเดินวนหาร้านถึง 40 นาที ความผิดพลาดเหล่านี้จึงเหมือนยืนยันว่าเพื่อนคิดถูก

items.stem: From the second week on, what did Nicha do before going somewhere?

items.stem: In paragraph 3, "which" in "which I'd always found awkward" refers to ____.
options: asking people for directions

items.stem: How does Nicha feel about map apps now?

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The Notebook
groups.text:
When Grandma Lek moved in with us, she brought only two boxes. One held her clothes. The other held a battered notebook with a cracked blue cover, its pages stiff with old splashes of fish sauce.

"My recipes," she said, as if that explained everything.

I was sixteen and confident in the kitchen, so one Saturday I decided to surprise her by cooking her famous tom kha, a chicken soup with coconut milk. I opened the notebook and immediately ran into trouble. Coconut milk: enough. Lime juice: depends on the day. Galangal: a good handful, not a greedy one. There wasn't a single exact measurement on the page.

I did my best. The soup was edible but flat, like a song played on the wrong instrument. Grandma tasted it, nodded politely, then shuffled over to the stove.

"Watch," she said. She squeezed in a little lime and tasted. She added a splash of fish sauce and tasted again. She never once looked at the notebook.

"Then why write it down at all?" I asked.

She smiled. "The notebook doesn't teach you the soup. It reminds you to pay attention."

These days I cook from that notebook most weekends. I still can't tell you how much coconut milk is enough. But I've stopped looking for the number.

items.stem: What was unusual about Grandma Lek's recipes?
options: They were in a foreign language.
They gave no exact amounts.
Most of the pages were missing.
They were copied from a cookbook.
They had no names for the dishes.
items.explanationTh: ผู้เล่าบอกว่า "There wasn't a single exact measurement on the page" สูตรเขียนเพียง "enough" หรือ "a good handful" ไม่มีปริมาณที่แน่นอน

items.stem: The soup was "like a song played on the wrong instrument." This suggests it was ____.

items.explanationTh: คำว่า "edible but flat" บอกว่าซุปกินได้แต่รสชาติไม่กลมกล่อม การเปรียบกับเพลงที่เล่นผิดเครื่องดนตรีจึงหมายถึงพอใช้ได้แต่ยังขาดบางอย่าง

items.stem: What does the narrator mean by "I've stopped looking for the number"?
options: She now weighs every ingredient carefully.

items.explanationTh: ผู้เล่ายังทำอาหารจากสมุดทุกสุดสัปดาห์ แต่ไม่พยายามหาปริมาณที่แน่นอนอีก แสดงว่ายอมรับวิธีทำอาหารแบบใช้การสังเกตของยาย

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Reading together, quietly
groups.text:
Most book clubs follow a familiar pattern: everyone reads the same novel at home, then meets to discuss it. In the small town of Bexley Vale, a group of librarians has turned that idea upside down.

At their monthly "Quiet Hour", members bring any book they like, whether a thriller, a cookbook or a comic, and read silently in the library's reading room for sixty minutes. There is no assigned title and no homework. Only after the hour is over do people chat, usually about whatever they happen to be reading.

The idea began almost by accident. Librarian Odette Fane noticed that many people who signed up for the traditional book club dropped out after one or two meetings. "They told me they felt guilty for not finishing the book," she explains. "Reading had become just another chore on their list."

Quiet Hour now attracts around forty regulars, from teenagers to retired farmers. Some admit they come mainly for the peace. "At home there's always a screen or a job waiting," says one member, who works night shifts at a bakery. "Here, for one hour, I'm allowed to do nothing but read."

Not everyone is convinced. Critics argue that without a shared book, the conversations stay shallow. Fane disagrees, though she accepts that the point is worth considering. "We're not trying to replace traditional clubs," she says. "We're offering a door for people who found the old one too heavy to push."

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A library that has stopped lending novels
A study of how quickly teenagers read
A traditional book club that meets every week
A book club that removes the pressure of a set title
A campaign to cut screen time at home
items.explanationTh: บทความเล่าถึง "Quiet Hour" ที่ให้สมาชิกนำหนังสืออะไรก็ได้มาอ่าน "There is no assigned title and no homework" จึงเป็นชมรมหนังสือที่ไม่กดดันเรื่องต้องอ่านเล่มที่กำหนด

items.stem: According to Odette Fane, why did people leave the traditional club?
options: The meetings were held too late at night.

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Talking about the weather, even when you aren't
groups.text:
Visitors to Britain often joke that the weather is the national hobby. Strangers at bus stops comment on the drizzle; colleagues open meetings by complaining about the wind. Some linguists suggest that in a country where the sky can change several times in one afternoon, the weather offers a safe, shared topic that does not require anyone to reveal personal information. Perhaps it is no surprise, then, that English is full of weather idioms which have nothing to do with the weather at all.

If you are feeling slightly unwell, you might say you are "under the weather". One popular explanation links the phrase to sailors, who were sent below deck, away from the rough weather above, when they felt seasick. When someone stays calm and keeps going through a difficult period, others may admire how they "weathered the storm". An argument that is "a storm in a teacup", meanwhile, causes far more fuss than it deserves.

Other idioms describe planning. To "save for a rainy day" means to put money aside for a future emergency, while "taking a rain check" politely postpones an invitation. The second phrase is believed to come from American baseball, where spectators at games cancelled because of rain received a ticket, or "check", to attend a later match.

Learners should be careful, however. "It's raining cats and dogs" appears in almost every textbook, yet many young British speakers rarely use it, preferring simply "It's pouring." Idioms, like the weather, change over time, and the best way to learn which ones are current is to listen to how people actually speak.

items.stem: According to the passage, why might the weather be such a popular topic in Britain?
options: It is a safe subject that everyone shares.
British people are trained to forecast it.
It lets strangers share personal news.
The British weather hardly ever changes.
Discussing it is a rule at most meetings.
items.explanationTh: ข้อความบอกว่าสภาพอากาศเป็น "a safe, shared topic that does not require anyone to reveal personal information" คือหัวข้อปลอดภัยที่ทุกคนมีร่วมกัน

items.stem: A friend says, "I can't come to the cinema tonight, but can I take a rain check?" She means that she ____.
options: needs to check the weather first
wants her ticket money back
has already seen the film

items.explanationTh: "take a rain check" คือการปฏิเสธคำชวนอย่างสุภาพโดยขอเลื่อนไปครั้งหน้า ตามที่บทความบอกว่า "politely postpones an invitation"

items.stem: Which situation is the best example of "a storm in a teacup"?
options: A team stays calm through a long losing season.

items.stem: The passage links the origin of "under the weather" to ____.

people waiting at rainy bus stops

items.explanationTh: บทความบอกว่า "One popular explanation links the phrase to sailors, who were sent below deck ... when they felt seasick"

items.stem: What does the writer suggest about the expression "It's raining cats and dogs"?
options: It means that the rain has suddenly stopped.

items.explanationTh: ผู้เขียนบอกว่าสำนวนนี้มีในตำราแทบทุกเล่ม แต่ "many young British speakers rarely use it" จึงอนุมานได้ว่าอาจฟังดูล้าสมัยสำหรับคนรุ่นใหม่

options: started an unnecessary argument

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The restless ground beneath us
groups.text:
Although the ground under our feet feels solid and still, Earth's outer shell is in constant, if extremely slow, motion. This shell, called the lithosphere, is broken into about fifteen major pieces known as tectonic plates. They rest on a hotter, softer layer beneath, the asthenosphere, and move at roughly the speed at which fingernails grow: a few centimetres a year.

Scientists did not always accept this idea. In the early twentieth century, the suggestion that continents could drift was widely dismissed, largely because no one could explain what force might move them. The evidence grew much stronger in the 1950s and 1960s, when surveys of the ocean floor revealed long underwater mountain ranges where new crust was forming, as well as matching patterns of magnetism in the rocks on either side.

Most geological activity happens at the boundaries between plates. Where plates move apart, molten rock rises to fill the gap and creates new crust. Where they collide, one plate may sink beneath the other in a process called subduction, which often produces deep ocean trenches and chains of volcanoes. Where two plates collide and neither sinks, the crust crumples upwards, which is how the world's highest mountain ranges formed. At a third type of boundary, plates slide past each other sideways; stress builds up along the boundary and is released suddenly as an earthquake.

Understanding these movements cannot prevent earthquakes, but it helps engineers decide where to build and how strong structures need to be.

items.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why the ocean floor has no mountains or volcanoes

How Earth's plates move and what happens where they meet

items.explanationTh: บทความอธิบายว่าแผ่นเปลือกโลกคืออะไร เคลื่อนที่อย่างไร และเกิดอะไรขึ้นที่รอยต่อแต่ละแบบ ตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นรายละเอียดผิดหรือขัดกับเนื้อเรื่อง

options: proved

items.explanationTh: ความคิดเรื่องทวีปเคลื่อนที่ไม่ได้รับการยอมรับ "because no one could explain what force might move them" dismissed จึงแปลว่าปฏิเสธ (rejected)

items.stem: The writer compares plate movement to the growth of fingernails to show that plates move ____.
options: faster than most people think

items.explanationTh: เล็บยาวขึ้นช้ามากแต่ไม่หยุด สอดคล้องกับ "in constant, if extremely slow, motion" คือเคลื่อนช้ามากแต่ต่อเนื่อง

items.stem: Which conclusion is supported by the last paragraph?
options: Knowing about plate boundaries can help reduce earthquake damage.

items.explanationTh: ย่อหน้าสุดท้ายบอกว่าความรู้นี้ "cannot prevent earthquakes, but it helps engineers decide where to build and how strong structures need to be" ซึ่งช่วยลดความเสียหายได้ แต่ไม่ได้หยุดแผ่นดินไหว

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: Why a scratched QR code still works
groups.text:
Square black-and-white QR codes now appear everywhere, from café menus to museum labels. Many people have noticed that a code can often still be scanned even when part of it is torn, dirty or covered by a sticker. This is not luck; it is design.

A QR code stores information as a pattern of tiny squares called modules, each representing a binary digit, either a 1 or a 0. The three large squares in the corners do not hold any data. Instead, they tell the scanner where the code is and which way up it is, so that it can be read from almost any angle.

The secret of the code's toughness is a technique called error correction. When a code is created, extra modules are added that contain no new information but describe the original data in a mathematical way. If some modules are damaged, the scanner uses these extra modules to work out what the missing ones must have been. Designers can choose from four levels of error correction. At the lowest level, about 7 per cent of the code can be restored; at the highest, about 30 per cent.

There is, however, a trade-off. The more error correction a code contains, the more modules it needs, so the code becomes larger or more crowded for the same amount of information. A code printed on a large outdoor poster, which may get wet or faded, benefits from a high level. A code on a small business card, which will usually be kept clean, can manage with less.

items.stem: What is the purpose of the three large squares in the corners?
options: To help the scanner locate the code and its position
To store the most important part of the data
To make the edges of the code look attractive
To show which level of error correction is used
To repair any modules that have been damaged

groups.instructionTh: อ่านข้อความ แล้วตอบคำถาม
groups.title: The food we never eat
groups.text:
Every year, a large share of the food produced around the world is never eaten. Estimates vary, but researchers agree that a surprising amount is lost or wasted somewhere between the farm and the plate. The problem is not only a moral one, as food is thrown away while many people still go hungry. It is also environmental. When food is wasted, so are the water, land, fuel and labour used to produce it, and food rotting in landfill releases methane, a powerful greenhouse gas.

Interestingly, where the waste happens depends heavily on a country's wealth. In lower-income countries, most food is lost early in the chain: crops spoil in the field because of poor storage, or go bad on the way to market without refrigerated transport. In wealthier countries, by contrast, the largest share is wasted at the end, in shops and, above all, in homes. Supermarkets may reject vegetables that are the wrong shape, and households buy more than they need, then throw it out once it passes a "best before" date, even though such food is often still perfectly fine.

Solutions therefore differ too. In some regions, simple technology such as airtight grain bags or solar-powered cold rooms can save a large part of a harvest. Elsewhere, the focus is on changing habits: planning meals, freezing leftovers and understanding date labels. In the city of Norhaven, for example, a pilot scheme gave 500 families a weekly meal-planning sheet; after six months, they reported throwing away about a quarter less food.

No single solution fits everywhere, but the aim is the same: making sure that food fulfils the purpose it was grown for.

items.stem: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Households can reduce greenhouse gases mainly by freezing their leftovers.
Where food is wasted varies with wealth, so the solutions vary as well.
Refrigerated transport is the most effective way to cut waste in rich countries.
Better date labels on packaging would prevent most of the world's food waste.
Wealthier countries now waste less food overall than poorer countries do.
items.explanationTh: บทความชี้ว่าจุดที่เกิดการสูญเสียอาหารขึ้นอยู่กับความมั่งคั่งของประเทศ และ "Solutions therefore differ too" ตัวเลือกอื่นเป็นรายละเอียดย่อยที่บิดเบือนหรือไม่ได้กล่าวไว้

items.stem: In lower-income countries, most food is lost ____.
options: after its best-before date
in restaurants and cafés
before it reaches consumers
in household kitchens
on supermarket shelves
items.explanationTh: บทความบอกว่าในประเทศรายได้ต่ำ "most food is lost early in the chain" เช่น เน่าในไร่หรือระหว่างขนส่งไปตลาด คือก่อนถึงมือผู้บริโภค

items.stem: Why is wasted food described as an environmental problem?
options: It attracts wild animals into large cities.
It makes farmland less fertile year after year.
It pushes up the price of fuel for drivers.
It reduces the amount of rain that farms receive.
The resources used to produce it are wasted as well.
items.explanationTh: ข้อความระบุว่า "When food is wasted, so are the water, land, fuel and labour used to produce it" และยังปล่อยก๊าซมีเทนด้วย

items.stem: The phrase "by contrast" in paragraph 2 could best be replaced by ____.

in addition
on the other hand
at the same time
for example

items.stem: What happened to the families in the Norhaven pilot scheme?
options: They saved exactly 500 meals a week.
They threw away about 25% less food.

They wasted a third more food than before.

items.explanationTh: บทความบอกว่าหลังหกเดือนครอบครัวเหล่านี้ "reported throwing away about a quarter less food" ซึ่งเท่ากับลดลงประมาณ 25%

items.stem: Which action best matches the advice given for wealthier countries?

items.explanationTh: สำหรับประเทศร่ำรวย บทความเน้นการเปลี่ยนพฤติกรรม เช่น "planning meals" การดูของในตู้เย็นก่อนจดรายการซื้อจึงตรงที่สุด ส่วนถุงเก็บเมล็ดพืชและรถห้องเย็นเป็นทางแก้ของประเทศรายได้ต่ำ
